overview:
The cap on ambiguity is a prompt rule, not code, in all three repos. Spec Kit's specify.md says: make informed guesses by default, and place at most 3 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: question] markers, only where (a) the choice significantly changes scope or UX, (b) several reasonable readings have different implications, and (c) no reasonable default exists. Ranking when more than 3 compete: scope > security/privacy > user experience > technical details. Excess unknowns are not marked; they become 'informed guesses' written under the spec's Assumptions section. A generated quality checklist (checklists/requirements.md) has an item 'No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain', and the model re-validates up to 3 iterations. Nothing in spec-kit's scripts counts markers (grep over scripts/src/tests finds none); the model both counts and enforces. Note a documentation conflict: spec-driven.md still says 'Don't guess: mark it', while the shipped specify.md says 'make informed guesses' and cap at 3. The command file wins in practice.

Spec Kit's clarify.md is the second stage: scan the spec against a 10-category taxonomy (Clear/Partial/Missing), keep an internal coverage map, build a queue of at most 5 questions ranked by Impact x Uncertainty, and ask exactly one at a time. Every question carries a model-chosen default: '**Recommended:** Option X - reasoning' for multiple choice (2-5 options in a table) or '**Suggested:** ...' for short answers (<=5 words). The user can reply 'yes'/'recommended'/'suggested' to take the default. Each accepted answer is written immediately: a bullet '- Q: ... -> A: ...' under '## Clarifications' > '### Session YYYY-MM-DD', plus an edit to the most appropriate spec section (functional requirement, data model, success criteria metric, edge case, terminology), replacing contradictory text. Termination: all critical ambiguities resolved, user says done/good/no more, or 5 asked. A coverage table (Resolved / Deferred / Clear / Outstanding) is printed at the end. This answers the owner's question: every clarify question has a default by construction, so 'accept recommended' is the unattended path, but spec-kit has no unattended mode and does not record that the default was taken rather than chosen.

OpenSpec and BMAD are looser but closer to unattended use. OpenSpec has no marker or cap: propose says ask only if ambiguity materially affects scope, externally observable behavior, compatibility or acceptance criteria; for minor details assume and record in the artifacts. Its design.md 'Open Questions' section is reserved for unknowns that can safely be answered later without changing specs, approach or task breakdown; anything that would change those must be asked now, and tasks stage re-checks Open Questions before writing tasks. BMAD has the most explicit headless contract: bmad-spec detects headless (no TTY, programmatic caller, or inputs pre-supplied) and then never asks; calls made without confirmation go to assumptions[], unfillable gaps to open_questions[], and thin input returns JSON {status:blocked, error_code:insufficient_intent}. All decisions are appended to an append-only .memlog.md (via memlog.py, types include assumption and question). bmad-build-auto ('one iteration of an unattended development loop') has the opposite posture to spec-kit: 'Do not fantasize or leave open questions. If the intent cannot be resolved, HALT with status blocked and the unresolved questions as blocking condition.'
howItWorks: Spec Kit /speckit.specify: load spec-template and constitution; extract actors/actions/data/constraints; for each unclear aspect, default to an informed guess recorded under ## Assumptions; add [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: specific question] only if scope/UX impact is significant AND multiple interpretations differ AND no reasonable default exists; hard limit 3 markers, ranked scope > security/privacy > UX > technical.

Spec Kit quality loop: write checklists/requirements.md (Content Quality, Requirement Completeness incl. 'No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain', Feature Readiness); validate; fix failures and re-validate up to 3 iterations, then document leftovers and warn the user.

If markers remain: if more than 3, keep the 3 most critical and convert the rest to informed guesses; render each as 'Question N' with a Context quote, the question, and a table of Options A/B/C/Custom with Implications; present all together; wait for 'Q1: A, Q2: Custom - ...'; replace each marker with the answer; re-validate.

Spec Kit /speckit.clarify (separate command, run before plan): run check-prerequisites script once for FEATURE_DIR/FEATURE_SPEC; load constitution; scan the spec against the taxonomy and build an internal coverage map; queue at most 5 candidate questions ranked by Impact x Uncertainty, dropping those that would not change implementation or validation, and tech-stack/method questions.

Ask one question at a time: '**Question:** <full interrogative>?' then a 'Why it matters' sentence, then '**Recommended:** Option X - reasoning' and an options table (or '**Suggested:**' and 'Format: Short answer (<=5 words)'). 'yes'/'recommended'/'suggested' accepts the default. Ambiguous replies get a disambiguation that does not count as a new question.

After each accepted answer: ensure '## Clarifications' and '### Session YYYY-MM-DD' exist; append '- Q: <question> -> A: <answer>'; apply the answer to the right section (FR bullet, data model, Success Criteria metric, Edge Cases, terminology normalised with '(formerly referred to as "X")'); remove contradicted text; save atomically after each answer.

Stop on: critical ambiguities all resolved, user says done/good/no more/stop/proceed, or 5 questions asked. If the quota is reached with high-impact categories left, list them as Deferred with rationale. Re-toggle only changed checkboxes in checklists/requirements.md and report before/after pass counts plus the coverage table (Resolved/Deferred/Clear/Outstanding).

Downstream: plan.md puts 'NEEDS CLARIFICATION' into Technical Context unknowns, runs Phase 0 research to resolve them, and says ERROR on unresolved clarifications; analyze flags placeholders (TODO, ???). All prompt-level.

OpenSpec propose: ask only on ambiguity that materially affects scope, observable behavior, compatibility, or acceptance criteria; otherwise assume and record in planning artifacts. design.md Open Questions are deferrable-only; tasks stage resolves any that would change what gets built. apply-change pauses on unclear tasks ('don't guess').

BMAD bmad-spec: classify headless vs interactive; headless defaults to 'express' (every gap becomes an open_questions[] entry); coherence pass moves unconfirmed calls into assumptions[]; each decision/assumption/question is appended to .memlog.md; spec is re-derived from the log; result is JSON {status, files[]}. bmad-build-auto step 1: resolve intent, otherwise HALT blocked with unresolved questions.

examples.label: specify.md: the cap rule (verbatim)
examples.text:
3. For unclear aspects:
   - Make informed guesses based on context and industry standards
   - Only mark with [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: specific question] if:
     - The choice significantly impacts feature scope or user experience
     - Multiple reasonable interpretations exist with different implications
     - No reasonable default exists
   - **LIMIT: Maximum 3 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers total**
   - Prioritize clarifications by impact: scope > security/privacy > user experience > technical details

examples.label: specify.md: excess markers become guesses; checklist loop (verbatim)
examples.text:
- **If items fail (excluding [NEEDS CLARIFICATION])**:
  1. List the failing items and specific issues
  2. Update the spec to address each issue
  3. Re-run validation until all items pass (max 3 iterations)
  4. If still failing after 3 iterations, document remaining issues in checklist notes and warn user

- **If [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain**:
  1. Extract all [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: ...] markers from the spec
  2. **LIMIT CHECK**: If more than 3 markers exist, keep only the 3 most critical (by scope/security/UX impact) and make informed guesses for the rest

examples.label: specify.md: reasonable defaults not to ask about (verbatim)
examples.text:
**Examples of reasonable defaults** (don't ask about these):

- Data retention: Industry-standard practices for the domain
- Performance targets: Standard web/mobile app expectations unless specified
- Error handling: User-friendly messages with appropriate fallbacks
- Authentication method: Standard session-based or OAuth2 for web apps
- Integration patterns: Use project-appropriate patterns (REST/GraphQL for web services, function calls for libraries, CLI args for tools, etc.)

examples.label: clarify.md: ranking and one-at-a-time constraints (verbatim)
examples.text:
4. Generate (internally) a prioritized queue of candidate clarification questions (maximum 5). Do NOT output them all at once. Apply these constraints:
    - Maximum of 5 total questions across the whole session.
    - Each question must be answerable with EITHER:
       - A short multiple-choice selection (2-5 distinct, mutually exclusive options), OR
       - A one-word / short-phrase answer (explicitly constrain: "Answer in <=5 words").
    - Only include questions whose answers materially impact architecture, data modeling, task decomposition, test design, UX behavior, operational readiness, or compliance validation.
    - Ensure category coverage balance: attempt to cover the highest impact unresolved categories first; avoid asking two low-impact questions when a single high-impact area (e.g., security posture) is unresolved.
    - Exclude questions already answered, trivial stylistic preferences, or plan-level execution details (unless blocking correctness).
    - Favor clarifications that reduce downstream rework risk or prevent misaligned acceptance tests.
    - If more than 5 categories remain unresolved, select the top 5 by (Impact * Uncertainty) heuristic.

examples.label: clarify.md: taxonomy (verbatim, condensed headings only)
examples.text:
Mark status per category: Clear / Partial / Missing. Categories:
1 Functional Scope & Behavior (goals, out-of-scope, roles)
2 Domain & Data Model (entities, identity/uniqueness, lifecycle/state, volume)
3 Interaction & UX Flow (journeys, error/empty/loading, a11y/l10n)
4 Non-Functional Quality Attributes (performance, scalability, reliability, observability, security & privacy, compliance)
5 Integration & External Dependencies (APIs + failure modes, import/export, protocol versioning)
6 Edge Cases & Failure Handling (negative scenarios, rate limiting, conflict resolution)
7 Constraints & Tradeoffs (technical constraints, rejected alternatives)
8 Terminology & Consistency (glossary, avoided synonyms)
9 Completion Signals (acceptance testability, measurable DoD)
10 Misc / Placeholders (TODO markers, ambiguous adjectives like 'robust', 'intuitive')
Add a candidate question for each Partial/Missing unless it would not materially change implementation or validation strategy, or concerns implementation method / tech-stack comparison / task breakdown.

examples.label: clarify.md: question format with Recommended default (verbatim)
examples.text:
- For multiple-choice questions:
   - **Analyze all options** and determine the **most suitable option** based on:
      - Best practices for the project type
      - Common patterns in similar implementations
      - Risk reduction (security, performance, maintainability)
      - Alignment with any explicit project goals or constraints visible in the spec
   - Present your **recommended option prominently** at the top with clear reasoning (1-2 sentences explaining why this is the best choice).
   - Format as: `**Recommended:** Option [X] - <reasoning>`
   - Then render all options as a Markdown table:

   | Option | Description |
   |--------|-------------|
   | A | <Option A description> |
   | B | <Option B description> |

   - After the table, add: `You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.`
- For short-answer style (no meaningful discrete options):
   - Provide your **suggested answer** based on best practices and context.
   - Format as: `**Suggested:** <your proposed answer> - <brief reasoning>`

examples.label: clarify.md: write-back rules (verbatim)
examples.text:
- For the first integrated answer in this session:
   - Ensure a `## Clarifications` section exists (create it just after the highest-level contextual/overview section per the spec template if missing).
   - Under it, create (if not present) a `### Session YYYY-MM-DD` subheading for today.
- Append a bullet line immediately after acceptance: `- Q: <question> → A: <final answer>`.
- Then immediately apply the clarification to the most appropriate section(s):
   - Functional ambiguity → Update or add a bullet in Functional Requirements.
   - Data shape / entities → Update Data Model (add fields, types, relationships) preserving ordering; note added constraints succinctly.
   - Non-functional constraint → Add/modify measurable criteria in Success Criteria > Measurable Outcomes (convert vague adjective to metric or explicit target).
   - Edge case / negative flow → Add a new bullet under Edge Cases / Error Handling.
   - Terminology conflict → Normalize term across spec; retain original only if necessary by adding `(formerly referred to as "X")` once.
- If the clarification invalidates an earlier ambiguous statement, replace that statement instead of duplicating; leave no obsolete contradictory text.

examples.label: clarify.md: termination and coverage summary (verbatim)
examples.text:
- Stop asking further questions when:
   - All critical ambiguities resolved early (remaining queued items become unnecessary), OR
   - User signals completion ("done", "good", "no more"), OR
   - You reach 5 asked questions.
- Never reveal future queued questions in advance.
- If no valid questions exist at start, immediately report no critical ambiguities.
...
- Coverage summary table listing each taxonomy category with Status: Resolved (was Partial/Missing and addressed), Deferred (exceeds question quota, or remaining item is specifically implementation method, tech-stack comparison, or task breakdown), Clear (already sufficient), Outstanding (still Partial/Missing but low impact).

examples.label: OpenSpec: ask vs assume, and Open Questions rule (verbatim)
examples.text:
If the request contains ambiguity that would materially affect scope, externally observable behavior, compatibility, or acceptance criteria, ask the user before creating the change. For minor details, make a reasonable assumption and record it in the planning artifacts.

- **Open Questions**: Unknowns that can safely be answered later without
  changing the specs, the approach, or the task breakdown. Omit if none.

Open questions are for genuinely deferrable unknowns, not decisions you
skipped. If a question would change the specs, the chosen approach, or
the task breakdown, resolve it now - ask the user instead of guessing.

examples.label: BMAD bmad-spec: headless mode detection and gap handling (verbatim)
examples.text:
4. Detect mode. **Headless** when any of: no TTY, programmatic caller (another skill or non-interactive runner), or the first message pre-supplies all inputs and asks for an artifact path back. **Interactive** otherwise.
...
When input is sparse, choose: **express** (best-effort distill, every gap becomes an `open_questions[]` entry) or **guided** (walk the five fields with the user one at a time). Headless defaults to express and logs the choice. Interactive asks.
...
Calls made without direct confirmation become `assumptions[]`; gaps that could not be filled become `open_questions[]`.

examples.text: 2. Resolve intent from the invocation prompt and loaded artifacts. Do not fantasize or leave open questions. If the intent cannot be resolved, HALT with status `blocked` and the unresolved questions as blocking condition.

examples.label: BMAD spec-template Assumptions / Open Questions sections (verbatim)
Worked example 1: spec after /specify (2 markers, 4 assumptions)
examples.text:
# Feature Specification: Shared Shopping Lists

## Requirements *(mandatory)*
- **FR-001**: Users MUST be able to create a list and invite others by link.
- **FR-004**: Invited users MUST be able to edit items [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: can invitees edit or only view? Impacts permissions model (scope)]
- **FR-007**: System MUST delete lists after [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: retention period for shared lists containing invitee names (privacy)]
- **FR-005**: Concurrent edits MUST show the latest saved state within 5 seconds.

## Assumptions
- Users have stable connectivity (informed guess; offline mode out of scope for v1).
- Authentication reuses the existing session login.
- Items are free text, max 200 chars (informed guess).
- Error messages are user-friendly with retry (default).

(A third potential unknown - 'sort order of items' - was NOT marked: UX detail, ranks below the cap, recorded as an assumption: 'manual order, newest last'.)

examples.label: Worked example 2: clarify questions as asked (one at a time)
examples.text:
**Question:** Should people who join a list through an invite link be able to change its items, or only view them? (FR-004)
Why it matters: decides whether the permission model needs roles and how acceptance tests are written.
**Recommended:** Option B - Editing by invitees is the common expectation for shared lists, and a single 'owner can revoke' role keeps the model small.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | View only; only the owner edits |
| B | Invitees can edit; owner can revoke access |
| C | Owner chooses per invitee |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.

> User: yes

**Question:** How long should a shared list be kept after its last edit before it is deleted automatically?
Why it matters: invitee names are personal data, so retention affects privacy compliance and storage.
**Suggested:** 12 months - common default for low-sensitivity consumer data.
Format: Short answer (<=5 words). You can accept the suggestion by saying "yes" or "suggested", or provide your own answer.

> User: 90 days

examples.text:

examples.label: Unattended design: assumptions ledger schema (proposed)
examples.source: illustrative (proposal for harness; BMAD .memlog.md and spec-kit Assumptions are the models)
examples.text:
# assumptions.md  (append-only; script-written; one fenced YAML record per item)
- id: A-007
  stage: specify|clarify|plan
  source: marker|queue|model-default        # how it arose
  question: "Can invitees edit or only view?"
  rank: scope|security|ux|technical|other   # spec-kit priority order
  options: ["view only","invitees edit; owner revokes","per-invitee"]
  chosen: "invitees edit; owner revokes"
  basis: recommended|spec-evidence|constitution|user-answer
  reasoning: "one sentence, quoting the spec/constitution line it rests on"
  confidence: high|medium|low
  reversible_cost: low|medium|high           # cost to change after build starts
  spec_refs: [FR-004]
  status: assumed|confirmed|overridden|blocking
  recorded_at: 2026-10-11T10:02:00Z

examples.label: Unattended design: marker-count gate (proposed)
examples.text:
# gate: no model judgement, pure script
count=$(grep -c '\[NEEDS CLARIFICATION' spec.md)
# rules (exit codes):
#   count > 3                      -> exit 2 'cap exceeded: convert excess to assumptions'
#   markers after stage 'clarify'  -> exit 3 'unresolved marker'
#   any ledger record status=blocking OR (rank in {security,scope} AND confidence=low AND reversible_cost=high) -> exit 4 STOP_AND_ASK (write question to inbox, halt)
#   ledger records != 'Clarifications' bullets + Assumptions bullets in spec.md -> exit 5 (unrecorded guess)
# any marker left in a spec marked final -> exit 6 (marker leakage)

pitfalls: Prompt-only enforcement: nothing in spec-kit code counts markers or caps questions; the cap of 3, the cap of 5, one-at-a-time, and 'keep the top 3, guess the rest' all rely on the model complying and counting correctly. Only the checklist file gives a checkable artifact, and the model fills it.

Silent guessing: the 4th and later unknowns are converted to 'informed guesses' in Assumptions with no record of the alternatives or the rank that justified dropping the marker. A reviewer sees only the winner. Also spec-driven.md says 'Don't guess' while specify.md says 'make informed guesses' - conflicting guidance.

Over-asking: clarify scans 10 categories and will find Partial items in most specs; the only brakes are the 5 cap and 'would not materially change' judgement. A model can burn all 5 on low-impact items or ask 3 specify markers then 5 clarify questions for the same thing. The 'Recommended' default also anchors users (rubber-stamping 'yes').

Marker leakage: markers can survive into the final spec if validation is skipped, hit the 3-iteration limit (leftovers only 'documented in notes and warn user'), or plan.md copies 'NEEDS CLARIFICATION' into Technical Context. plan says ERROR on unresolved clarifications, but that is a prompt, not a gate.

Accepted default is indistinguishable from a chosen answer: clarify records '- Q: ... -> A: ...' whether the user typed it or said 'yes' to the model's recommendation. No provenance, no confidence, no reversal cost.

Taxonomy and checklist cost: scanning 10 categories every run and a 16-item checklist re-toggle add tokens and rewrite churn; much of the precise formatting (table alignment warnings, 'Question must end with ?', exact reply phrases) compensates for weaker models.

Unattended mode is absent from spec-kit: 'Wait for user to respond' is hard-coded, so an unattended run either stalls, or the model self-answers inventing the user's choice. BMAD solves with headless detection but its detection is itself prompt logic (no TTY, programmatic caller).
BMAD memlog/spec is cleaner but 'express' headless can fill open_questions[] with everything and push the decision downstream; thin input only blocks via the model's judgement of 'too thin'.
OpenSpec 'material' and 'deferrable' are judgement calls with no marker, no count, and no gate: 'minor details: assume and record' has no required record location beyond 'planning artifacts'.
modelEra: Claude 5-era models do not need most of the scaffolding. Compensating-for-weak-models features to drop or shrink: (1) the exhaustive 10-category taxonomy plus an internal Clear/Partial/Missing map (a 5-generation model can read the spec and find the load-bearing gaps without enumerating categories); (2) hard formatting policing: table-alignment warnings ('CRITICAL - Table Formatting'), the 'Question must end with ?' and 'NEVER use a topic label' rules, the exact reply-phrase list ('yes', 'recommended', 'suggested'), and 'Never reveal future queued questions'; (3) the 3-iteration validation loop and re-toggle-only-changed-checkboxes diff rules; (4) 'Make informed guesses' reminders and the list of reasonable defaults, since a strong model defaults sensibly. Keep: the numeric caps as policy (they are product decisions, not compensation), the priority order scope > security/privacy > UX > technical, the Impact x Uncertainty rule, the 'recommended + reasoning' format (it is what makes unattended acceptance possible), the write-back-to-section rule, and the coverage/deferred report. The single-writer, append-only log of BMAD (memlog) and its HALT/blocked statuses are structural, not model-weakness compensation, and are the part worth borrowing. Caveat: stronger models tend to guess confidently rather than over-ask, so the main 5-generation risk is silent assumption, not over-asking; that is addressed by a ledger plus script gate, not by prompt wording.
whatWouldChange: 1) Make the marker cap and the stop rule script-owned: a gate script greps the spec for '[NEEDS CLARIFICATION' (count > 3 refuses; any marker remaining after the clarify stage refuses; a final spec with any marker refuses). 2) Replace 'ask the human' by 'record, then apply the recommended default' in unattended mode: each clarify question is emitted as structured data (question, rank, options, recommended, reasoning, confidence, reversible_cost) and the script writes an assumptions.md record with status=assumed and basis=recommended; the model never edits the ledger directly, and the spec's Clarifications bullet gets an '(assumed)' tag so default-accepted answers are distinguishable from user answers. 3) Stop-and-ask rule, computed by the script from ledger fields and not by the model: halt (and write the question to an inbox) when a record has rank in {security, scope} AND confidence=low AND reversible_cost=high, or the question has no defensible option (the 'no reasonable default exists' leg of specify.md), or the same question is re-opened after being assumed (contradiction). Everything else proceeds with the default. 4) Collapse specify and clarify into one stage with one queue: a single pass ranks unknowns by Impact x Uncertainty with the spec-kit priority order; the top 3 are marker candidates, the next up to 5 become recorded assumptions, the rest are noted as deferred in the ledger (not as silent guesses). 5) Keep the Assumptions section in the spec derived from the ledger (render, don't hand-edit; BMAD's derive-from-log pattern) so the two cannot drift. 6) Add a back-propagation check: when later stages (plan/implement) contradict an assumed record, set status=overridden and re-open dependent steps. 7) Drop the long taxonomy, formatting rules and 3-iteration loop; keep a short list of what must be decided versus defaulted, per the Claude-5 guidance. 8) Add a test per route: an unattended run with a seeded high-risk unknown must exit via the stop-and-ask route and the exit must be accepted by the real gate.
